title: Review: Oxidation states and half-equations; Orbitals and electron configuration; Covalent and dative bonding; Lewis structures; Bond enthalpies
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EN03#t2 term and clue written for the game; AS04#t3 term and clue written for the game; AS04#t1 term and clue written for the game; AS04#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AS04#N.6a, BD02#N.11, EN03#N.10a, RX01#N.14, AS04#N.12a, BD02#N.12b, RX01#N.13, AS04#N.9a, BD02#N.2, RX01#N.6a, AS04#N.3a, RX01#N.11a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Endothermic
items.clue: Describes the breaking of a bond: energy is absorbed.

items.label: Orbital
items.clue: A region around the nucleus where an electron is likely to be found; not a path.

items.label: Hund's rule
items.clue: Electrons enter regions of equal energy singly, with parallel spins, before pairing.

questions.stem: Which full electron configuration of a ground-state atom is correct?

options.text: scandium: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 4p¹
cobalt: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁹
iron: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁶ 4s²
germanium: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹² 4s²

questions.explanation: 18 electrons to 3p⁶, then 4s², then six in 3d: 26 in all.

questions.stem: Ammonia, NH₃, reacts with a hydrogen ion, H⁺, to form the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺. Which statement about the bonds in NH₄⁺ is correct?

options.text: The bond formed from the lone pair on nitrogen is longer and weaker than the other three N–H bonds
The new bond formed from a pair of electrons supplied by the H⁺ ion to nitrogen
The new bond formed from one electron supplied by nitrogen and one electron supplied by H⁺
All four N–H bonds are identical, although one formed from the lone pair on nitrogen

questions.explanation: The new bond is co-ordinate: both electrons from N. Once formed, all four N–H bonds have the same length and strength.

questions.stem: CH₄(g) + Cl₂(g) → CH₃Cl(g) + HCl(g), ΔH = −99 kJ mol⁻¹. Bond enthalpies / kJ mol⁻¹: C–H 413, Cl–Cl 243, H–Cl 432. What value for the C–Cl bond enthalpy do these data give?

options.text: 125 kJ mol⁻¹
755 kJ mol⁻¹
323 kJ mol⁻¹
162 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.explanation: One C–H and one Cl–Cl break (656 kJ); one C–Cl and one H–Cl form. 656 − (x + 432) = −99, so x = 323 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: In the thermite reaction, aluminium reacts with iron(III) oxide: Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → Al₂O₃(s) + 2Fe(l). What happens to the iron?

options.text: It loses electrons: iron is always oxidised when it reacts, as it does in rusting.
It gains electrons: its oxidation number falls from +3 to 0, and aluminium supplies them.
It loses electrons to aluminium, since aluminium gains the oxygen during the reaction.
It gains electrons: its oxidation number falls from +6 to 0, as Fe₂O₃ has two Fe atoms.

questions.stem: A ground-state phosphorus atom is [Ne] 3s² 3p³. Where are its three 3p electrons?

options.text: Together in one 3p orbital, which all three share.
On one circular orbit at a fixed distance from the nucleus.
Two paired in one 3p orbital, one in a second, the third left empty.
One in each of the three 3p orbitals, with parallel spins.

questions.explanation: Three equal-energy orbitals, three electrons: one each, spins parallel. Each electron is spread over its dumbbell-shaped region.

questions.stem: Carbon monoxide, CO, has 10 outer electrons, the same as N₂. Like N₂, it has a triple bond and one lone pair on each atom. Which describes the three shared pairs?

options.text: Three ordinary covalent bonds: C and O each supply three electrons.
Two ordinary covalent bonds, plus one co-ordinate bond from C to O.
Three co-ordinate bonds, all from O to C.
Two ordinary covalent bonds, plus one co-ordinate bond from O to C.

questions.explanation: C shares two electrons and O two: two ordinary pairs. O then donates one lone pair to C: C≡O with an arrow O→C. Each atom keeps one lone pair and has 8.

options.text: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂
2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂
NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O

questions.explanation: O in H₂O₂ is −1 (a peroxide). It goes to −2 in H₂O (reduced) and to 0 in O₂ (oxidised): one element in one species, both ways.

questions.stem: An iron atom (Z = 26) has the condensed electron configuration [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². How is an Fe²⁺ ion formed from this atom?

options.text: Two of the six 3d electrons are removed from the atom.
One 4s electron and one 3d electron are each removed.
Two electrons are added to the 3d sub-shell of the atom.
Both of the 4s electrons are removed from the atom.

questions.explanation: Transition metal atoms lose 4s electrons before 3d: [Ar] 3d⁶, 24 electrons.

questions.stem: What holds the hydrogen atom and the chlorine atom together in a molecule of hydrogen chloride, HCl?

options.text: The need of each atom to gain a full outer shell by sharing a pair of electrons
The shared pair of electrons itself, acting as a physical link between the atoms
The electrostatic attraction of both nuclei to a shared pair of electrons
The electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions H⁺ and Cl⁻

questions.explanation: The shared pair lies between the H and Cl nuclei and is attracted to both. That attraction is the covalent bond.

questions.stem: Chlorine reacts with aqueous iron(II) ions: 2Fe²⁺(aq) + Cl₂(aq) → 2Fe³⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq). Which species is the oxidising agent in this reaction?

options.text: Fe²⁺, since it loses electrons and so is itself oxidised
Cl₂, since it gains electrons and so is itself reduced
Cl⁻, since it is the species holding the gained electrons
None, since no species here gains or loses any oxygen atoms

questions.explanation: Chlorine's oxidation number falls from 0 to −1: each Cl₂ gains two electrons from Fe²⁺. The species that accepts electrons is the oxidising agent.

questions.stem: What is the maximum number of electrons that a 3d sub-shell can hold, and why?

options.text: 20 electrons, as its ten orbitals can each hold two electrons of opposite spin
18 electrons, as the n = 3 shell holds a maximum of 2n² electrons
10 electrons, as its five orbitals can each hold two electrons of opposite spin
2 electrons, as the 3d sub-shell is one orbital that holds a single pair

questions.explanation: Five orbitals × two electrons of opposite spin = 10.

questions.stem: In acidic solution, MnO₄⁻(aq) is reduced to Mn²⁺(aq) and Fe²⁺(aq) is oxidised to Fe³⁺(aq). In the balanced overall redox equation, what amount of Fe²⁺ reacts with 1 mol of MnO₄⁻?

options.text: 1 mol
5 mol
2 mol
3 mol

questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 to +2, so each MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons; each Fe²⁺ loses 1. The iron half-equation is multiplied by 5.
